findings.pdf_says: 14.9.51.3   Syntax rules  (printed in the same bold sub-clause style as 14.9.51.1 General and 14.9.51.2 General formats on page 815)
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.51.3 Syntax rules   (H2, while its siblings on page 815 are '### 14.9.51.1 General' and '### 14.9.51.2 General formats')
findings.why_it_matters: A four-level clause number (14.9.51.3) is promoted to the same heading level as the statement clause itself (## 14.9.51 WRITE statement). The syntax rules stop being nested inside the WRITE statement clause, which breaks the document outline, any TOC generated from it, and any tooling that resolves a citation like '14.9.51.3' by walking the heading tree. ISO_COBOL.md line 33010 (and 33074 for 14.9.51.4, on a later page) carry the same defect.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote to '### 14.9.51.3 Syntax rules' (ISO_COBOL.md line 33010) to match 14.9.51.1/.2. Sweep 14.9.51.4 at line 33074 in the same change.

findings.pdf_says: 15.19.3   Argument rules  /  15.19.4   Returned value rules  (printed in the same bold sub-clause style as 15.19.1 General and 15.19.2 General format on page 859)
findings.markdown_says: ## 15.19.3 Argument rules  and  ## 15.19.4 Returned value rules   (both H2, while '### 15.19.1 General' and '### 15.19.2 General format' on page 859 are H3)
findings.why_it_matters: The two rule sub-clauses are lifted out of the CONVERT function clause and become siblings of '## 15.19 CONVERT function'. The neighbouring function 15.20 COS is transcribed correctly ('### 15.20.3 Argument rule', '### 15.20.4 Returned value rule'), so CONVERT is the outlier and any outline- or citation-resolving tool will mis-parent CONVERT's argument and returned-value rules.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote both to H3 in ISO_COBOL.md (lines 34597 and 34620) so they read '### 15.19.3 Argument rules' and '### 15.19.4 Returned value rules', matching 15.20.3/15.20.4.

findings.pdf_says: FUNCTION CONVERT ( argument-1 source-format destination-format )  — BOTH 'FUNCTION' and 'CONVERT' carry an underline in the printed general format (verified by rendering page 859 at 300 dpi and cropping the line: two separate underline rules sit beneath FUNCTION and beneath CONVERT).
findings.markdown_says: <u>FUNCTION</u> CONVERT ( argument-1 source-format destination-format )   (ISO_COBOL.md line 34553 — only FUNCTION is wrapped in <u>…</u>; CONVERT is left plain)
findings.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2 an underlined word is a REQUIRED word and a non-underlined word is an OPTIONAL word that may be omitted without changing the meaning. Marking FUNCTION underlined but CONVERT not asserts a positive (and false) distinction: it reads as though 'FUNCTION ( argument-1 … )' were legal. Every sibling function in clause 15 uses the '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>NAME</u>' form (ABS, ANNUITY, ATAN, COMBINED-DATETIME, CONCAT, CURRENT-DATE, …), so CONVERT is the outlier. The identical defect exists at line 38293 for TEST-NUMVAL.
findings.suggested_repair: Change ISO_COBOL.md line 34553 to '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>CONVERT</u> ( argument-1 source-format destination-format )'. Sweep the sibling defect at line 38293 (<u>FUNCTION</u> TEST-NUMVAL) in the same change set.

findings.pdf_says: Format 2 (reporting):  USE [ GLOBAL ] BEFORE REPORTING identifier-1  — USE, GLOBAL, BEFORE and REPORTING are all underlined (required words); only identifier-1 is not.
findings.markdown_says:
Format 2 (reporting):

USE [ GLOBAL ] BEFORE REPORTING identifier-1   (ISO_COBOL.md line 32562 — bare prose, no code fence, and no 'Figure notes' paragraph, unlike Formats 1, 3 and 4 on the same page which each carry one)
findings.why_it_matters: Formats 1, 3 and 4 on this page each record which words are underlined in a Figure-notes paragraph; Format 2 records nothing, so the required-word marking on BEFORE and REPORTING is simply absent. A reader or generator applying the page's own convention would infer that no word in Format 2 is required, i.e. that 'USE REPORTING identifier-1' or 'USE BEFORE identifier-1' is legal.
findings.suggested_repair: Put Format 2 in a fenced block like its siblings and add a Figure-notes line: 'USE, GLOBAL, BEFORE and REPORTING are underlined in the printed standard (required words); identifier-1 is not. [ GLOBAL ] is optional.'
